content.text: Sequencing executes statements once in order. Selection chooses which statements to execute. But many real tasks require repeating a set of steps — counting through numbers, processing every item in a list, or repeating until some condition changes. Iteration is the third and final building block of every algorithm. It allows a block of statements to execute multiple times without writing those statements repeatedly.

content.definition: A repeating portion of an algorithm. Iteration repeats a specified number of times or until a given condition is met.

content.text: Iteration statements change the sequential flow of control by repeating a set of statements zero or more times, until a stopping condition is met. The word 'zero or more' is important — it is possible for a loop body to execute zero times if the stopping condition is met before the loop even begins.

content.definition: An iteration statement that executes the block of statements exactly n times.

content.text: REPEAT n TIMES is the simpler of the two iteration statements. Use it when you know exactly how many times you want the block to repeat before the loop begins. The block always executes exactly n times — no condition is checked, it simply counts.

content.code:
-- Basic REPEAT n TIMES:
REPEAT 4 TIMES
{
   DISPLAY "hello"
}
-- Executes exactly 4 times
-- Output: hello hello hello hello

-- Using REPEAT n TIMES to build a sum:
sum ← 0
i ← 1
REPEAT 5 TIMES
{
   sum ← sum + i
   i ← i + 1
}
DISPLAY sum

-- Trace:
-- Before loop: sum=0, i=1
-- Iteration 1: sum=0+1=1, i=2
-- Iteration 2: sum=1+2=3, i=3
-- Iteration 3: sum=3+3=6, i=4
-- Iteration 4: sum=6+4=10, i=5
-- Iteration 5: sum=10+5=15, i=6
-- Output: 15  (1+2+3+4+5)

content.definition: An iteration statement that repeats the block of statements until the Boolean condition evaluates to true. If the condition is true initially, the loop body is not executed at all. If the condition never becomes true, an infinite loop occurs.

content.text: REPEAT UNTIL repeats the block of statements until the Boolean condition evaluates to true. The condition is checked BEFORE each execution of the loop body. This means: if the condition is already true when the loop is first encountered, the loop body executes ZERO times. If the condition never becomes true, the loop runs forever — an infinite loop.

content.code:
-- Basic REPEAT UNTIL:
i ← 1
REPEAT UNTIL(i > 5)
{
   DISPLAY i
   i ← i + 1
}

-- Condition checked BEFORE each iteration:
-- Check: i=1, (1>5)=false → execute body: display 1, i becomes 2
-- Check: i=2, (2>5)=false → execute body: display 2, i becomes 3
-- Check: i=3, (3>5)=false → execute body: display 3, i becomes 4
-- Check: i=4, (4>5)=false → execute body: display 4, i becomes 5
-- Check: i=5, (5>5)=false → execute body: display 5, i becomes 6
-- Check: i=6, (6>5)=true  → STOP, loop ends
-- Output: 1 2 3 4 5

content.text: Critical Rule: Condition Already True Before Loop Starts

content.term: What happens when REPEAT UNTIL condition is already true?
content.definition: The loop body is not executed at all, because the condition is checked before the loop begins.

content.text: This is the most commonly tested subtlety about REPEAT UNTIL. Because the condition is checked BEFORE the loop body executes, if the condition is already true when the loop is first reached, the body never executes — not even once. The program simply skips the entire loop and continues.

content.code:
-- Condition already true BEFORE loop starts:
x ← 10
REPEAT UNTIL(x = 10)
{
   x ← x + 1     -- this NEVER executes
   DISPLAY x      -- this NEVER executes
}
DISPLAY x         -- displays 10

-- x=10, condition (x=10) is already true
-- Condition is checked first → true → loop body skipped entirely
-- x remains 10 throughout
-- Output: 10

-- ------

-- Compare: condition starts false, becomes true after several iterations
y ← 1
REPEAT UNTIL(y > 5)
{
   y ← y + 1
}
DISPLAY y   -- displays 6
-- Condition is false at start → body executes, eventually y=6, 6>5=true → stops

content.label: Exam Tip
content.text: REPEAT UNTIL checks the condition BEFORE executing the loop body. If the condition is ALREADY TRUE when the loop starts, the body executes ZERO times — it is completely skipped. This surprises many students who expect 'until' to mean 'at least once.' In AP CSP pseudocode, REPEAT UNTIL does not guarantee even one execution.

content.definition: Occurs in REPEAT UNTIL iteration when the ending condition will never evaluate to true, causing the loop to repeat forever.

content.text: An infinite loop occurs when the ending condition in a REPEAT UNTIL loop never becomes true. This typically happens in two ways: the loop variable is never updated inside the body (so the condition can never change), or the update logic causes the variable to skip over the target value entirely.

rows: x starts at 0, adds 2 each time, condition x=5
x starts at 0, adds 1 each time, condition x=5
count never updated inside loop body, condition count=5
count never changes so condition never becomes true
Condition is already true — body never executes
x starts at 1, adds 1, condition x > 100

content.label: Common Mistake
content.text: Forgetting to update the loop variable inside a REPEAT UNTIL loop is the most common cause of infinite loops. If the variable that determines the condition never changes, the condition can never become true. Always check: is there something inside the loop body that will eventually make the condition true?
Comparing REPEAT n TIMES vs REPEAT UNTIL

content.term: Compare: REPEAT n TIMES vs REPEAT UNTIL
content.definition:
REPEAT n TIMES: repeats a fixed number of times, always executes the block at least once if n > 0.
REPEAT UNTIL: repeats until a condition becomes true, may not execute at all if the condition is already true.

rows: Until condition is true — could be 0, 1, or many
Yes — if condition is already true when loop starts
No — always terminates after exactly n
Yes — if condition never becomes true
When you know exactly how many times to repeat
When you repeat until something happens — unknown number of repetitions

content.text: Just like conditionals, iteration statements change the sequential flow of control. Without loops, statements execute exactly once in order. With loops, the same block of statements can execute many times before the program moves on. Understanding iteration as a flow-control mechanism — not just a counting tool — is essential for writing and reading programs correctly.

content.code:
-- Combining iteration with selection:
count ← 0
i ← 1
REPEAT UNTIL(i > 10)
{
   IF(i MOD 2 = 0)
   {
      count ← count + 1
   }
   i ← i + 1
}
DISPLAY count

-- Counts even numbers from 1 to 10:
-- i=1: 1 MOD 2 = 1 ≠ 0, skip
-- i=2: 2 MOD 2 = 0, count=1
-- i=3: skip. i=4: count=2. i=5: skip. i=6: count=3
-- i=7: skip. i=8: count=4. i=9: skip. i=10: count=5
-- i=11: (11>10)=true → loop stops
-- Output: 5

content.text: Like selection, iteration can be expressed without using a programming language. Natural language descriptions of loops appear on the AP exam — you must be able to recognize iteration in plain English and translate it to pseudocode, or read pseudocode and describe it in natural language.

rows: Keep adding 1 to x until x is greater than 100
While the count is less than 10, increment the count and display it
REPEAT UNTIL(count ≥ 10) { count ← count + 1; DISPLAY count }
For each student in the roster, display their name
FOR EACH student IN roster { DISPLAY student }

content.text: Summary: What to Know for the Exam

items: Iteration is a repeating portion of an algorithm — repeats a specified number of times or until a condition is met
Iteration statements change the sequential flow of control by repeating a set of statements zero or more times until a stopping condition is met
REPEAT n TIMES executes the block exactly n times — no condition checked, always terminates
REPEAT UNTIL(condition) repeats the block until the condition evaluates to true — the condition is checked BEFORE each iteration
If the condition in REPEAT UNTIL is already true when the loop starts, the body executes ZERO times
An infinite loop occurs in REPEAT UNTIL when the ending condition never evaluates to true
Common causes of infinite loops: loop variable never updated inside body, or update logic causes variable to skip over the target value
REPEAT n TIMES: use when you know exactly how many repetitions are needed
REPEAT UNTIL: use when you repeat until something changes — unknown number of repetitions
Iteration can be expressed in natural language, diagrams, and pseudocode — all describe the same repeating process
